pumac-2007-finals-b-01.prompt: Let $C$ and $D$ be two points, not diametrically opposite, on a circle $C_1$ with center $M$. Let $H$ be a point on minor arc $CD$. The tangent to $C_1$ at $H$ intersects the circumcircle of $CMD$ at points $A$ and $B$. Prove that $CD$ bisects $MH$ iff $\angle AMB=\frac\pi2$.
pumac-2007-finals-b-01.answer: Both conditions are equivalent to: the reflection of $M$ in $H$ lies on the circle $CMD$.
pumac-2007-finals-b-01.reviewNote: No official answer key was published for PUMaC 2007; the answer was worked out independently.

pumac-2007-finals-b-02.prompt: Suppose that $A$ is a set of positive integers less than $N$ and that no two distinct elements of $A$ sum to a perfect square. That is, if $a_1,a_2\in A$ and $a_1\ne a_2$ then $|a_1+a_2|$ is not a square of an integer. Prove that the maximum number of elements in $A$ is at least $\lfloor\frac{11}{32}N\rfloor$.
pumac-2007-finals-b-02.answer: Take all $n<N$ whose residue mod $32$ lies in $\{1,5,9,10,13,14,17,21,25,29,30\}$.
pumac-2007-finals-b-02.reviewNote: No official solution. The standard mod-32 construction proves the bound for every N except N congruent to 9 mod 32 (one element short when elements must be less than N); no uniform patch found. A computer search confirms the claim itself for all N up to 63.
